newsitem.title: UK: Jones Stroud plummets on H1 profit fall.
newsitem.headline: Jones Stroud plummets on H1 profit fall.

text.p: Shares in Jones Stroud (Holdings) Plc plummeted on Thursday after the textile and electrical accessories manufacturer posted a drop in first-half profits.
The shares were quoted 50p down at 375p by 1152 GMT.
Jones Stroud said pre-tax profits dropped to 2.85 million stg in the first half ended September 30 from 3.64 million stg last year, on turnover which rose to 41.09 million stg from 40.46 million.

Chairman Philip Jones said the drop in profits was due to a seasonal decline in demand for Wykes' stretch yarns, supplied to the knitwear and hosiery industries, compared with the record levels during the hot summer of 1995.
Jones also said the company's Australian wing, Jones Stroud Pty. Ltd, had suffered as a result of fierce competition in a depressed market.
While admitting disappointment with the results, Jones said: "There are signs that the markets we serve are improving".
"But the results for the year as a whole will depend upon the level of the recovery at Wykes and the effect of difficult trading conditions in Australia," he added.
